text:
support_jess: customer reported sudden p99 spikes for /v1/generate starting ~18:12 UTC, multiple requests returning 504s and long tails. customer id=acme-inc, sample req_id=req_9a8b7c6d, region=us-west-2. They say it started after a deploy but timeline fuzzy. attaching logs below.

mike_s: looking. any alerts?

oncall-bot: alert: inference-p99-us-west-2 >= 1200ms (count 42) at 18:15 UTC — incident-id: INC-20247

anya: got the customer's request/response traces (redacted). I can see a pattern: many small prompts (~<32 tokens) with a spike in queue_time and batch_hold_time. p95 OK, p99 bad. Suggests batching hold window got longer for tiny requests.

samir: can you paste the active continuous-batcher config for that cluster? I want to check hold_window_ms and adaptive settings.

anya: paste: ```json
{ "mode": "continuous", "hold_window_ms": 12, "min_batch_size": 4, "max_batch_size": 64, "adaptive": true, "adaptive_target_latency_ms": 50, "max_wait_ms": 300 }
```

support_jess: customer also shared that traffic pattern is lots of tiny chat messages from many users (hundreds of concurrent), previously fine. They rolled a minor runtime change at 18:00.

mike_s: hypothesis: adaptive hold logic overshot for many tiny-requests, increasing hold_window to aggregate bigger batches but causing tail p99 for small prompts because some paths hit max_wait or priority inversion.

anya: I pulled historical hold-window histograms — at 17:50 median 10ms, at 18:05 median jumped to 80ms for small-prompts bucket. There's a correlation with a downstream KV-cache miss rate spike. Could be KV cache pressure causing dequeue delays and skewing adaptive estimator.

samir: can we reproduce locally? try replaying small-prompt trace against canary with current batcher flags. run: ```bash
# run on canary (us-west-2-canary)
curl -X POST https://canary.redwood.internal/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $CANARY" -d '{"prompt":"hi","max_tokens":10}' -s -D - -o /tmp/out -w "\nSTATUS:%{http_code} TIME:%{time_total}s\n" | tee replay.log
```

mike_s: I started a small replay with ~2000 tiny requests/second and saw p99 jump to 1.6s when adaptive was enabled. When I forced hold_window_ms=8 (disable adapt) p99 dropped to 240ms. so adaptive algo is the main suspect.

support_jess: customer asked for a temporary mitigation while we root cause. they can accept a config change on their Dedicated pool.

anya: mitigation options: 1) roll back adaptive=true -> set adaptive=false + hold_window_ms=8 (safe lower latency) 2) patch adaptive estimator to ignore cache-related dequeue jitter (requires PR) 3) enable per-tenant small-prompt fast-path that bypasses batching for prompts < 32 tokens. 4) route affected traffic to lower-latency reserved pool.

samir: immediate: i'll push a config override on the Dedicated pool for acme-inc to adaptive=false, hold_window_ms=8. doing a canary apply now.

oncall-bot: deploy-job: started config-update for pool acme-inc-dedicated by samir @ 18:28 UTC — job-id cfg-9273

mike_s: after override canary tests show p99 back to 210-260ms. on main cluster measured customer request p99 dropped from ~1.6s to ~230ms within 2 minutes.

product_lina: customer is ok with temporary config change if we commit to follow up. please document impact on throughput/cost.

anya: follow-ups: - PR to adaptive estimator to factor out cache-miss jitter (owners: eng-runtime) - add telemetry that reports hold_window_ms distributions by prompt-length bucket - run small-prompt fast-path experiment (eng-platform + eng-runtime) - Ops runbook: automated mitigation toggle to disable adaptive per-pool.

samir: filed ticket INF-5432 with details + timeline + revert steps. assigning to eng-runtime (mike_s, anya).

support_jess: relayed to customer — they confirmed latency improved and will monitor. leaving ticket open until patch. :thumbsup:

mike_s: quick notes for postmortem: root cause likely interaction between adaptive batching estimator and transient KV cache miss surge that increased dequeue jitter; estimator interpreted longer dequeue times as need to increase hold, amplifying latency for tiny prompts.

anya: saving logs and traces to incident folder: s3://redwood-incident-archive/INC-20247/ — includes histograms, canary replay, config diffs.

samir: closing the live incident alert. will reopen if we see recurrence.

oncall-bot: alert-resolved: inference-p99-us-west-2 — resolved at 18:36 UTC (auto)
